charles-ethiopic: R. H. Charles, The Ethiopic Version of the Book of Enoch, Anecdota Oxoniensia (1906)
laurence-enoch: Richard Laurence, The Book of Enoch the Prophet (1821; Ge'ez text 1838)
stuckenbruck-enoch91: Loren T. Stuckenbruck, 1 Enoch 91–108, Commentaries on Early Jewish Literature (2007)
vanderkam-enoch-growth: James C. VanderKam, Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition, CBQ Monograph Series 16 (1984)
boccaccini-parables: Gabriele Boccaccini, ed., Enoch and the Messiah Son of Man: Revisiting the Book of Parables (2007)
erho-stuckenbruck-manuscript: Ted M. Erho and Loren T. Stuckenbruck, "A Manuscript History of Ethiopic Enoch," Journal for the Study of the Pseudepigrapha 23 (2013): 87–133
reed-fallen-angels: Annette Yoshiko Reed, Fallen Angels and the History of Judaism and Christianity: The Reception of Enochic Literature (2005)
dalton-proclamation: William J. Dalton, Christ's Proclamation to the Spirits: A Study of 1 Peter 3:18–4:6, 2nd ed. (1989)
elliott-1peter: John H. Elliott, 1 Peter, Anchor Bible 37B (2000)
vanderkam-adler-heritage: James C. VanderKam and William Adler, eds., The Jewish Apocalyptic Heritage in Early Christianity (1996), with VanderKam's chapter on 1 Enoch in early Christian literature
nicephorus-stichometry: The Stichometry of Nicephorus, a list of books with their lengths attached to the Chronography of Nicephorus, patriarch of Constantinople (early 800s)
decretum-gelasianum: Decretum Gelasianum, a Latin list of books to be received and not received, credited to Pope Gelasius I (probably compiled in the 500s)
syncellus-chronography: George Syncellus, Chronography (about AD 810), trans. William Adler and Paul Tuffin, The Chronography of George Synkellos (2002)
bonner-epistle: Campbell Bonner, The Last Chapters of Enoch in Greek (1937)
black-enoch-greek: Matthew Black, ed., Apocalypsis Henochi Graece, Pseudepigrapha Veteris Testamenti Graece 3 (1970)
bruce-travels: James Bruce, Travels to Discover the Source of the Nile, 5 vols. (1790)
athenagoras-plea: Athenagoras, A Plea for the Christians (about AD 177)
africanus-chronography: Julius Africanus, Chronography (about AD 221), surviving in fragments quoted by later writers
chrysostom-genesis: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Genesis, homily 22 (about AD 388)
alexander-3enoch: P. Alexander, trans., "3 (Hebrew Apocalypse of) Enoch," in J. H. Charlesworth, ed., The Old Testament Pseudepigrapha, vol. 1 (1983)
ephrem-genesis: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis (about AD 360s)
brakke-festal39: David Brakke, "A New Fragment of Athanasius's Thirty-Ninth Festal Letter: Heresy, Apocrypha, and the Canon," Harvard Theological Review 103 (2010): 47–66, with an English translation of the whole letter
hilary-psalms: Hilary of Poitiers, Tractates on the Psalms (about AD 360s), on Psalm 132 (133 in English Bibles)
origen-john: Origen, Commentary on the Gospel of John, book 6 (about AD 231–235)
dfg-enoch-edition: Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft project 270668285, Text-critical Edition and Translation of 1 Enoch, results report (gepris.dfg.de), with publications by Loren T. Stuckenbruck, Ted M. Erho and others
